dialect.detail: Uses SCREEN SECTION with LINE/COL clauses and AUTO attribute, consistent with GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL) or similar open-source COBOL compiler targeting terminal-based screen I/O

purpose.domain_detail: Academic group project: a student information system menu shell covering student records, course records, schedules, instructor records, building records, and reports
purpose.summary: MAIN-MENU is a terminal-based interactive menu program for a student information system. It presents a main menu and sub-menus for students, courses, schedules, instructors, buildings, and reports, dispatching to sub-programs via CALL or nested PERFORM. It is a group project from 2014.

notable_features: SCREEN SECTION with LINE/COL positioning and AUTO attribute
Date/time display via ACCEPT FROM DATE and ACCEPT FROM TIME
CALL to external subprograms (STU-BUILDER, COURSE-MASTER, COURSE-ADD, COURSE-UPDATE, COURSE-INQUIRY, COURSE-LIST)
Nested paragraph structure (210-STUDENT defined inside 200-MAIN indentation, likely a coding error)
verdict.notes: The program is clearly a student group project (author and date in header comments, 2014). Paragraph 210-STUDENT appears to be indented as if nested inside 200-MAIN but COBOL paragraphs are not truly nested; this is a common student mistake. Several sub-menus (schedule, building, instructor, reports) incorrectly PERFORM 210-STUDENT instead of their own logic, suggesting incomplete implementation. Dialect is likely GnuCOBOL based on SCREEN SECTION usage, but could also be Micro Focus or ACUCOBOL; no compiler-specific directives present to disambiguate.
